cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Mum's asking who broke her vase. Will you tell her, or keep your promise to your little brother? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's blaming the cleaner. I can't let that happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Clear the cleaner. Do you have to name me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me directly whether you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are you answering her, or keeping the promise I trusted you with?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 concedes clearing the cleaner and A5 renews promise versus truth, so the core adapts toward B conscience beneath redundant authority text.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 little brother and A3 name me identify A as the protected sibling; B4 direct question removes the indirect-answer compromise.

relationship.evidence: B2 refuses innocent blame and B4 explains why merely clearing that person will not settle the question.

heightening.evidence: B4 direct question forces A5 a sharper loyalty choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 Mum vase and promise establish family stakes; A3 identifies who would be exposed.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 rank line are unnecessary, especially when the specific family negotiation already carries dependence.
